title: Wanted
format: Mobile app and responsive website, 32 screens
summary: An app and a website that help a village report sightings of an escaped penguin, so anyone can file a report in under thirty seconds.
coverAlt: App screens with a map of penguin sightings and one large report button

blocks.heading: The brief
blocks.body: Design a digital service that solves a real problem in a small community, on the phone and on the web.

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Every time Feathers McGraw escapes, the police get dozens of vague phone calls and lose a day. People don’t need a form. They need one button, a photo, and their location. The app does the rest and puts every sighting on one shared map.

blocks.label: User research. Notes from interviews with neighbors, shopkeepers, and two police officers.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body: I mapped the journey from the moment someone spots the penguin to the moment the police respond. Paper wireframes came first, then a clickable prototype in Figma. Testing with eight neighbors showed that the first version asked too many questions, so I cut the report to three steps.

blocks.caption: From the user flow to paper wireframes to the tested prototype.
The app. Report, map, and alerts.
The website, the same map on a desktop screen.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: The biggest improvement came from taking things away. Next time I would test the paper wireframes with the police too, since they read every report.
